_comment: Population anchors for the Hong Kong avifauna timeline. NOTHING HERE IS SMOOTHED: anchors are the source of truth and everything between them is derived at build time. Each anchor carries a 'basis' - 'documented' means the figure appears in a cited survey or report and the 'source' field names it; 'estimated' means it is a placeholder used only to span a gap and MUST NOT be presented as fact. The viewer draws estimated stretches dashed and says so on screen. See docs/data-research-prompt.md for how the real figures are being sourced.

_metrics._comment: Abundance in Hong Kong is not recorded the same way for every bird, and pretending otherwise is the easiest way to lie with this piece. Waterbirds get counted in Deep Bay; passerines do not, and are known instead from passage counts or from atlas occupancy. Each species therefore declares which metric its numbers are, and the viewer scales and labels accordingly instead of putting a duck flock and a bunting passage count on one axis.

species._data_status: PLACEHOLDER ANCHORS - awaiting sourced figures. Documented context so far: global population fell by an estimated 84-95% between 1980 and 2013 (Kamp et al. 2015, Conservation Biology), and IUCN uplisted the species Least Concern (2004) -> Vulnerable (2008) -> Endangered (2013) -> Critically Endangered (2017). Those are GLOBAL, not Hong Kong figures, and are not used as anchors here. Hong Kong needs peak autumn passage counts from HKBWS records and Long Valley monitoring.
